DICOM Services, Objects, Transfer Syntaxes, Validation, Tools, and Other Integration

Unit 2: Clinical Engineering. Lesson 12 of 65 in CIIP Academy.

A modality sends a study and PACS rejects every image. The network is fine. The association opened, but the presentation context was refused. This is a transfer syntax problem, and it shows up often.

Services and objects the pair negotiates

A modality and PACS must agree on the SOP classes (the object types) and on a transfer syntax for each. A device may support the class but offer only a syntax the PACS cannot read.

Transfer syntaxes

Syntax                     Meaning
Implicit VR little endian  the default every device must support; uncompressed
Explicit VR little endian  uncompressed; each element states its type
JPEG lossless              compressed, every pixel recovered
JPEG 2000                  wavelet; lossless-only and lossy variants exist

If no proposed syntax is acceptable, that context is rejected and the objects are not sent. The fix is to enable a common syntax on one side, not to resend.

Validation

Validation checks an object against the standard: required elements present, valid values, correct UIDs. Run it before accepting a new device and when imported studies behave oddly.

Tools at recognition level

A set of tools helps: an echo and send utility, a query tool, a header dump viewer, a simulator that acts as a modality or PACS, a validator, and network capture that shows the association messages.

Other integration types

Secondary capture wraps a screenshot as an image object. An encapsulated PDF stores a document in a DICOM study. Non-DICOM converters turn photos or video into DICOM objects so they can be filed with a patient.

Exam tip: association rejected points to the AE title; association opened but images refused points to the SOP class or transfer syntax.
Remember
Modality and PACS must agree on SOP classes and a transfer syntax, and when no syntax matches the context is rejected, so check the negotiated list before blaming the network.
Deeper explanation

DICOM Services, Objects, Transfer Syntaxes, Validation, Tools, and Other Integration, explained slowly

Matching what two devices can speak

Two devices can open an association and still fail to move an object. The fault is in what was negotiated for that SOP class.

Transfer syntax          Compression     Reversible?     Typical use
Implicit VR little end.  none            n/a             default every device supports
Explicit VR little end.  none            n/a             most uncompressed exchange
JPEG lossless            yes             yes             archive and exchange
JPEG 2000 lossless only  yes             yes             archive
JPEG 2000                yes             lossless or lossy   review or archive
JPEG baseline            yes             no (lossy)      review copies
RLE lossless             yes             yes             some ultrasound and secondary capture

A worked negotiation

A scanner offers CT image storage with JPEG 2000 only. The PACS accepts CT image storage with implicit and explicit little endian only. No syntax matches, so the context is rejected and the scanner reports that the store failed with no image sent. Two fixes: enable explicit little endian on the scanner so the pair has one syntax in common, or enable JPEG 2000 on PACS if the vendor supports it. The network, the title, and the port are not the cause.

Validation

Validating an object means checking it against the standard. A validator will tell you that a required element is missing, a value does not fit its type, or a UID is malformed. Validate a sample from each new device before you accept it, and validate an imported study that behaves oddly.

Tools

Tool                 Use
Echo and send        test a connection, push a file
Query tool           test a find and retrieve
Header dump          read tags and spot wrong values
Simulator            stand in for a modality or PACS before the real one arrives
Validator            check conformance
Network capture      see the association and rejection reasons

Other integration types

A secondary capture stores a screen image as a DICOM image, which has no original pixel data to remeasure. An encapsulated PDF stores a document inside a DICOM study. A non-DICOM converter wraps a photo or video, takes the patient from a worklist or typed entry, and files it as DICOM, so the weak link is how the patient is chosen.
